attributes.residual: real 32, target 78 / ours 78 instructions, opcode multiset IDENTICAL (0t) - a pure permutation plus a recolor, and the mechanism is named. (1) SCHEDULE, one instruction: `addi r28,r4,0` (homing the arg1 parameter into callee-saved r28) is emitted at 0x30 in ours, BEFORE `stw r0,232(r31)`, and at 0x34 in the target, AFTER it. (2) REGISTER_ONLY, the coupled recolor: the target writes the gPlayers low half to a FRESH volatile register (`addi r5,r3,gPlayers@lo ; add r31,r5,r6`), which frees the @ha temp r3 for the loop counter, giving p->r5, i->r3, idx*0x335C->r6; ours folds the low half in place (`addi r3,r3,gPlayers@lo ; add r31,r3,r5`), so p stays in r3 and the counter is pushed to r4, giving p->r3, i->r4, offset->r5. The two halves are one joint decision; 15 regnorm RENAMING rows follow from it. NOTE the two sides also SWAP which symbol gets the in-place fold: the target folds lbl_80284878 in place and writes gPlayers fresh, ours does the reverse. NOT WEBFRANK-ELIGIBLE: tools/gdl/webfrank_audit.py --grep game/ui/select reports exactly one eligible function in the TU and it is init_player_select (the existing pin), not init_player_change; the audit requires identical instruction shape and the one-slot permutation breaks that precondition. Per claim.law.addrlo-inplace-lever-needs-a-paid-copy-and-its-population-is-empty.20260901.v1 this function no longer pays a copy at all, so the lever has nothing left to remove here. TOOLING NOTE: regnorm reports COUNT-MISMATCH with 2 unpaired rows, but both are the SAME instruction `addi r28,r4,0` at 0x38 versus 0x3c - positional pairing fabricated the mismatch across the schedule drift, exactly the hazard AGENTS.md warns about; the aligned view is authoritative and shows 78/78 with an identical multiset.
